# Laya post-processing fixtures

`rl_agent_config.json` is the unmodified checkpoint configuration from
[`convaiinnovations/laya`](https://huggingface.co/convaiinnovations/laya/blob/fd4f9dbcf4fde222fd43174bdd4c3b08b789e4e1/rl_agent_config.json)
at revision `fd4f9dbcf4fde222fd43174bdd4c3b08b789e4e1` (SHA-256
`ae287b56bbcf5f8c4f4541ae9dfd00c914c4c48b940b8398c3058af37ba92bbd`).

`postprocessing_reference.json` contains independent Python standard-library
calculations for fixed synthetic logits, using the same temperature bucket,
softmax, typed output and entropy formulas as the checkpoint's
[`rl_agent_api.py`](https://huggingface.co/convaiinnovations/laya/blob/fd4f9dbcf4fde222fd43174bdd4c3b08b789e4e1/rl_agent_api.py)
and `rl_common.py`. It does not contain model outputs or weights. The upstream
model card declares Apache-2.0; this is not an inference accuracy benchmark.
Regenerate it with `python tests/fixtures/generate_reference.py`.

`sequence_reference.json` was produced by running the unmodified
`serialize_state`, `render_options` and `build_sequence` functions from the
same pinned `rl_common.py`, using a deterministic test tokenizer (each
character's Unicode value plus 1000, with CLS=101, SEP=102, MASK=103). It covers
choice, score, noul, marker text removal, head truncation and left-truncated
state. It is not a substitute for testing the published tokenizer.
To reproduce it, download the pinned `rl_common.py` linked above and run
`python tests/fixtures/generate_sequence_reference.py path/to/rl_common.py`;
the generator verifies the upstream file's SHA-256 before use.

`head_reference.json` is generated by executing the pinned `DecisionModel`
class itself with synthetic fixed encoder outputs and deterministic weights.
The test encoder supplies hidden states; the upstream learned head remains
unmodified. Cases exercise the two Transformer layers, padded and unpadded
sequences, two or three option markers, all three question types, and one or
two attention heads. It includes both raw logits and the probabilities obtained
using the published checkpoint's temperatures. No model weights are included.
Regenerate using PyTorch 2.15 with
`python tests/fixtures/generate_head_reference.py path/to/rl_common.py`; the
generator checks its SHA-256 before running.

`checkpoint-head-header.json` lists the 35 non-encoder head tensors in the
same pinned revision's [`model.safetensors`](https://huggingface.co/convaiinnovations/laya/blob/fd4f9dbcf4fde222fd43174bdd4c3b08b789e4e1/model.safetensors).
Every listed tensor is stored as F16. The 21,536-byte original JSON header
has SHA-256 `3a42d8e7a96d5aa22c5bc9475d7ff092e32a832ae7c6973688f66f7a84048c04`.
The full checkpoint also contains the encoder and an F32 temperature buffer.

`real-head-reference.json` was generated with the actual F16 head weights,
decoded to f32, and deterministic *synthetic* encoder outputs. It records
choice and score cases with different marker counts and padding. The upstream
`DecisionModel` head is executed directly in PyTorch. The standalone Rust
f32 comparison had maximum absolute errors of `3.9e-6` for option
logits and `0.0015` for action logits (whose magnitudes exceed 2,500 in
these synthetic cases); option-probability error was below `1.8e-7`. This is
not an end-to-end checkpoint or BF16 qualification.

To reproduce, obtain the pinned `rl_common.py` and complete `model.safetensors`
and run the following from this Component repository. The generator verifies
the source, header and relevant weight bytes by SHA-256, writes decoded weights
outside the repository, and creates the small reference JSON separately:

```sh
python tests/fixtures/generate_real_head_reference.py \
  --source /path/to/rl_common.py --model /path/to/model.safetensors \
  --out /tmp/laya-head-f32 --reference /tmp/laya-reference.json
MAGNETAR_LAYA_HEAD_F32_DIR=/tmp/laya-head-f32 cargo test --release --locked \
  --test head_integration decoded_checkpoint_head_matches_upstream_pytorch -- --ignored
```

The generator also accepts `--header`, `--start` and `--end` instead of
`--model` for individually retrieved byte ranges. Model weights and decoded
weight files are not checked into this repository.
